title: Ambient flow of people at Pyrkon 2026: real walking in a crowd
description: A 3½-minute handheld portrait video of a convention hall at Pyrkon 2026 in Poland: hundreds of people walking, standing, turning and weaving past each other at their own pace, shared on Wikimedia Commons under CC BY 4.0.

authors.name: Rose Abrams
authors.note: Wikimedia Commons contributor who filmed it on a 2026 trip to Poland

summary:
## What it is

A video file on Wikimedia Commons, *Pyrkon 2026 - ambient flow of people 1.webm*, filmed by the Commons user Rose Abrams on 20 June 2026 ("photos from my 2026 Poland trip", own work). It runs 205 seconds and was shot handheld in portrait at the Pyrkon fan convention in Poznań: one of the fair's large exhibition halls (hall 5A, a high steel roof, a bare concrete floor), seen from inside a slowly moving crowd. Its licence is **Creative Commons Attribution 4.0** (CC BY 4.0). Commons serves it as the original (843 MB) and in smaller transcodes; the 480p VP9 transcode was used here.

## Key points

- Hundreds of real people on foot, many in costume, in one continuous take: walking alone and in groups, starting, stopping, turning on the spot to look, standing and talking, carrying bags, props and costume pieces.
- People pass the camera at every distance, from a full figure a couple of metres away to dozens of small figures across the hall, so both a single gait and a crowd's flow are visible.
- The pace is that of a busy indoor event: unhurried walking, frequent short stops and changes of direction, rarely running.
- A wide range of builds, ages and footwear, from trainers to platform boots and long costumes, each changing how a person walks.
- No narration, just ambient sound; the camera wanders and turns with the crowd.

## The topic

Animators have always studied real people to make characters move believably, from Muybridge's photographic sequences (1880s) to rotoscoping and, today, motion capture. A reference video does what a capture file cannot: it shows a gait in context, with clothes, bodies and other people, and lets a viewer judge whether something reads as human at a glance. The cues that give an animated walk away are well known: feet that slide or float, a metronomic rhythm with every step alike, arms swinging in lockstep with the legs, a body that bobs without settling its weight, starts and stops with no lean into them, and crowds where everyone moves at the same pace. A crowd filmed as it is shows the opposite: every person a slightly different tempo and stride, weight shifting before a turn, steps shortening as people slow, idle sway while standing, a hand raised to wave to a friend across the hall, a bag hitched up on a shoulder mid-stride.

CC BY 4.0 lets the video be shown and reused, commercially too, with credit to its author, a link to the licence and an indication of changes (here, a 20-second cut, scaled to 540 pixels high, without sound).

## For Maia City

Intent 99b612ec's last check (c7) asks Samuel whether Stand-in and Elder woman, now on the VRM humanoid skeleton and moving by motion capture, move like real people. Their 20-second film from the render bench is shown beside the first 20 seconds of this video, so the comparison is with ordinary people walking, stopping and turning in a crowd, not with another animation. Credit: Rose Abrams, *Pyrkon 2026 - ambient flow of people 1*, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0.
